title: Indexed state scan over a pointer range
summary: Recovered the read-only stdcall predicate at VA 0x53c7c0. It ignores its first stack argument, scans a signed-length 32-bit pointer range, and returns AL true for state 6 or 7 at object + 0xd4 + index*100. Arithmetic wraps at 32 bits. Direct callers at 0x4a7aed and 0x4a903b pass an enclosing object's +0x58 descriptor.
test_description: Differential GCC i386 calls against the original-address oracle: states 0,1,5,6,7,8,0xffffffff,0x80000006 at every position; negative, zero, positive and multiply-wrapping indices; empty, reversed, signed-negative and partial-byte ranges; early match followed by null entries. Checks descriptor, capacity, pointer entries and every fixture object word remain unchanged after each implementation and original call; varies ignored argument.
known_limits: Enclosing object and indexed record semantic names are unresolved; state record stride is 100 bytes and state field offset is 0xd4 from the object plus indexed stride.
Descriptor and entries deliberately retain original 32-bit address layout; native 64-bit integration needs an explicit address/layout adaptation.
Invalid dereferenced addresses retain original preconditions and are not exercised. Exception paths are absent in this routine. Only Boolean AL is recovered; other EAX bits are unspecified.
Behavioral recovery only; no matching-byte claim.
